findings.title: KeyError when Integration metadata lacks 'sender'
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the re-install path does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. `sender` is only stored in metadata when it is present in pipeline state (`build_integration` only adds it `if state.get("sender")`), and Integrations created before sender tracking existed (or where the installation webhook was missed) will not have a `sender` key in metadata at all. For any such pre-existing Integration that has no OrganizationIntegration (the exact path this new check runs on: 'OrganizationIntegration does not exist, but Integration does exist'), this raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of the failure dialog. Use a guarded lookup (e.g. `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")`) and treat a missing sender as a verification failure rather than crashing.

findings.title: No test for the state-signature mismatch path
findings.body: The PR description states the pipeline now fails 'If there is a mismatch between state parameter supplied by user and pipeline signature', which is a core security property of this change (CSRF protection on the OAuth callback). The added tests cover the user-mismatch and installation-not-found cases, but no test exercises `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` with a wrong/absent-but-present `state` value to assert the failure page is rendered and the flow aborts. A regression removing or weakening the signature check would not be caught by the test suite.
